To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• For the proximal stochastic-gradient method, the convergence rate of the iterates to the minimizer of the time-averaged function is independent of the initialization.

(1) the tracking efficiency of stochastic proximal methods is logarithmic in the initialization quality, (2) the tracking efficiency is linear in the number of iterations, (3) iterate averaging is sufficient to obtain high probability guarantees, (4) the tracking efficiency depends on the variance of the drift process, and (5) the tracking efficiency can be made arbitrarily small with the appropriate step-decay scheduling

(1) the tracking efficiency of proximal stochastic gradient methods with step-decay is logarithmic in the initialization quality, (2) the tracking efficiency is linear in the time drift, and (3) high probability convergence guarantees can be obtained by using a step-decaying learning rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of minimizing an unknown and time-varying convex function.
the design of algorithms that achieve fast and reliable convergence to the minimizer of a convex function that evolves in time according to stochastic and unknown dynamics.
the problem of minimizing convex functions that change in time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proximal stochastic algorithm with iterate averaging and a step-decaying schedule is a very efficient algorithm for tracking a time varying function, with convergence guarantees that hold both in expectation and in high probability, and that are independent of the initial point.
the convergence of stochastic gradient methods with iterate averaging is not affected by time drift, and in fact is not much affected by stochasticity either.
the tracking efficiency is logarithmic in the initial error, which is a significant improvement over the linear dependence in the literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to make the stochastic optimization algorithms robust to time drift, and that the robustness can be achieved with a simple step-decay scheme.
we provide the first high probability convergence guarantees for stochastic optimization under time drift and we establish that iterate averaging is the optimal strategy to achieve this goal.
, in the presence of drift, iterate averaging is not only necessary but also sufficient to guarantee high-probability convergence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tracking efficiency is independent of the rate at which the function changes.
stochastic optimization algorithms can be used to solve tracking problems with a high probability guarantee, and without the need to know the drift rate in advance.
the tracking performance of a stochastic algorithm with iterate averaging can be improved by simply increasing the number of iterations.
